shipped_rows.title_o: Brand Experience: What is It? How is it Measured? Does it Affect Loyalty?

blind_target.title: Eco-Friendliness in the Brand Experience of High-Tech Products.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In this study we replicate the extended BXS [19] cross-nationally to measure differences in the ways consumers experience the eco-friendliness of global smartphone brands in a cross-national context. The survey items were selected from the previously developed and extended BXS [18,19,107]. We assess the four items measuring eco-friendliness as well as the other four brand experience dimensions from the BXS by conducting structural equation modeling (SEM) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) following the same steps that Brakus et al. [18] undertook.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The findings of our study indicate that the eco-friendliness dimension can be generalized in two countries with very different demographics and economic situations.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The earlier eco-friendliness dimension is explicitly retested and confirmed in both countries; changes to the other dimensions do not negate this target finding.

prior_decision.quote: In this study we replicate the extended BXS [19] cross-nationally to measure differences in the ways consumers experience the eco-friendliness of global smartphone brands in a cross-national context.
prior_decision.location: Research Method and Data, line 49 (and Reference 19, line 273)
prior_decision.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests the eco-friendliness BXS extension developed in Saari (2016) [19], which had previously only been confirmed in one Western country, and confirms its construct validity and reliability across both Finland and India.

luna_triage.reason: The candidate is the separately cited Saari (2016) thesis that introduced the eco-friendliness extension, and the source explicitly says that extension is replicated cross-nationally. Shipped row 592 is Brakus et al. (2009), the foundational BXS paper, not Saari (2016); the source also cites Brakus [18] and Saari [19] as distinct works. Prior adjudication explicitly confirms this target as missing, and the supplied source and row support that distinction.
